DEFINITIONUnder administrative direction of the Modesto Junior College President, the Executive Director serves as the chief fundraising officer for Modesto Junior College and the Modesto Junior College Foundation. The Executive Director provides leadership, both directly and through supervision of Foundation staff, for the planning and implementation of a comprehensive development program.

The Executive Director sets ambitious, clear, and achievable goals, and inspires the staff, as well as the Board of Directors to meet and exceed expectations. The Executive Director is responsible for the identification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship of donor prospects (individuals, Foundations, and corporations), gift funds, scholarships, and donor records at all levels of giving. The Executive Director of the Modesto Junior College Foundation will place special emphasis on the cultivation and solicitation of major gift donors and grant-makers capable of giving $10,000 and above.

The Executive Director also collaborates with the Foundation Board of Directors and the MJC President to advance fundraising and community partnership initiatives consistent with the Foundation’s mission.

SUPERVISION RECEIVED AND EXERCISED

Qualifications

Receives administrative direction from the Modesto Junior College President; may also receive and respond to directives from the Chancellor and/or Modesto Junior College Foundation Board of Directors, as needed. Provides direct supervision over Foundation support staff and various others who may be hired to support Foundation work. Supervises initiatives and events consistent with the Foundation’s mission.Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree in an unrelated field coupled with at least five years in development and community relations may be accepted if it is addressed in the applicant’s cover letter.
Experience: Minimum of three years of recent, successful development experience.

Preferred Qualifications

Masters or Doctorate in business, education, public administration, public relations, development management, or related fields.
Senior level development experience in a college or university setting.
Preference is for the Executive Director to have a thorough understanding of best practices in fundraising, with demonstrated success with annual fund, major gifts, alumni relations, estate and planned gifts, corporate and/or Foundation fundraising

jobs.title: Program Director, Center of Innovation
jobs.description:
Who We Are

We are Tennis! The USTA (United States Tennis Association) is the national governing body for the sport of tennis and the leader in promoting and developing the sport’s growth on every level in the United States, from local communities to the crown jewel of the professional game, the US Open.

The USTA Foundation Incorporated (USTAF or USTA Foundation) is the social impact arm of the United States Tennis Association Incorporated (USTA), utilizing the powerful combination of tennis and education to enhance the lives of under-resourced youth through its support of the National Junior Tennis & Learning (NJTL) network. For more than 50 years, NJTL has impacted thousands of under-resourced youth across the nation, and today the network features more than 270 chapters that reach more than 233,000,000 young people from under-resourced communities annually.

Why Work for the USTA?

We are a passionate team of staff and volunteers focused on growing the sport of tennis and making it accessible to all. We are committed to removing barriers and creating opportunities for ALL to participate.

About Lulu's Place

Lulu's Place will offer state-of-the-art facilities in Los Angeles, north of LAX airport, between the communities of Westchester and Playa del Rey, bringing together academic, athletic, and wellness programs for youth from all backgrounds. Trusted partners, including TGR Foundation, a Tiger Woods charity; the United States Tennis Association (USTA) and its charitable arm, USTA Foundation; Cedars-Sinai; and Providence will bring together professional teachers, coaches, mentors, and service providers to deliver high-quality programs to children and their families.

The vision for this project is rooted in the passion and generosity of Carol "Lulu" Kimmelman, a Southern California native, former elementary school teacher in South Los Angeles, and lifelong tennis player who passed away in 2017 after a courageous battle with ovarian cancer. Today, her husband, Doug Kimmelman, and their four children honor Lulu's legacy by advancing her mission to transform young people's lives and create greater equity in sports and education through this groundbreaking youth center.

The Role

The Program Director at Lulu’s Place will lead a youth development program focused on college and career readiness and non-degree career pathways, operating within a shared facility alongside several partner organizations. This position involves a managerial component, overseeing program staff and volunteers.

Operational Oversight: Manage day-to-day operations for USTAF Center of Innovation (CoI), ensuring all activities align with the foundation’s mission, goals, priorities, and safety standards.
Partner Integration: Lead coordination efforts with Lulu's Place Leadership, TGR Foundation, and other on-site program partners to successfully align on shared goals and execution of educational and tennis programming.
Program Development: Lead design and oversee the planning and implementation for direct day, weekend, and afterschool programming. The programs will incorporate the core principles of the NJTL network, tennis, education, and mentorship
Community Engagement: Sets the strategy and is responsible for the USTAF CoI engagement with local community partners, including greater LA NJTL organizations, school districts, charter schools, youth development organizations, and other key community stakeholders.
Quality Assurance: Responsible for the oversight and delivery of USTAF programs and partnered programs to accomplish established and shared goals.
Strategic Growth: Identify opportunities to test and expand programs/products to increase the reach and enhance the impact of NJTL sports-based interventions within the community.

Partner & Facility Coordination

Stakeholder Liaison: Serve as the primary point of contact for diverse community partners, including non-profits, schools, and local NJTL organizations.
Facility Scheduling: Work with the Lulu’s Place facility team and partners to manage the complex master calendars for shared facility use, balancing USTAF programming needs with Lulu's Place partners and community access.
Collaborative Governance: Represent the USTAF by attending all regular partner meetings to ensure effective, efficient communication, align priorities, and minimize confusion and conflicts.
Resource Allocation: Responsible for the USTAF offices and footprint at Lulu's Place.

Impact Measurement & Reporting

Data Collection: Implement systems to track participant attendance, demographic data, and youth development outcomes across all partner programs.
Align with the USTAF leadership in the development of the “measures of success” and align with Lulu's Place partners to align on shared goals

Reporting: Capture and deliver program data into reports for foundation leadership, donors, and community stakeholders.
Evaluation: Use qualitative and quantitative feedback to assess the effectiveness of the "collective impact" model at the facility site.

Compliance & Administration

Safety & Risk Management: Ensure all partners and staff meet Safe Play compliance per the USTA requirements, including regular training and background checks. Ideally, all USTAF staff and program partners will be CPR/First Aid certified, including AED.
Budget Oversight: Manage the USTAF operational budget in collaboration with the leadership of the Programs and Services team of the USTA Foundation.
Grant Compliance: Assist partners in meeting the reporting requirements and performance benchmarks tied to USTA Foundation Program activities and funding
Ensure the program's compliance with all applicable Lulu’s Place youth safety policies, background check requirements, and licensing standards
Establish and oversee data collection, record-keeping, and reporting systems for student participation and outcomes across all program functions
Oversee vendor and service provider relationships (transportation, curriculum materials, technology, etc.)
In addition to the stated compliance and administration duties, review and maintain organizational policies and procedures, updating as needed to reflect best practices and legal requirements
Manage three full-time direct reports

Who You Are

Education: A bachelor’s degree in a related field such as Sports Management, Recreation Administration, Education, Social Work, or Non-Profit Management is required.
Work Experience: 5 to 7 years of experience in program coordination, youth development, or sports administration. Tennis background and/or understanding of the tennis environment is preferred.
Partner Management: Proven track record of managing relationships with community partners, schools, or diverse local organizations is required.
Safety Certifications: Valid CPR, First Aid, and AED certifications (or the ability to obtain them within 30 days of hire) are required.
Clearance: Ability to pass comprehensive, recurring federal and state background checks to work with minors is required.
Technical Proficiency: Strong skills in Microsoft Office Suite (especially Excel), Google Workspace, and familiarity with project management or participant tracking software are required.
Valid driver’s license and reliable transportation for travel between facility sites is required.
Schedule Flexibility: Ability to work non-traditional hours, including evenings and weekends, to align with youth sports schedules is required.
Physical Stamina: Ability to be mobile and active on sports courts or fields for extended periods and lift/move equipment up to 50 lbs is required.

What We Offer

At the USTA, we know people are our most important asset. For this reason, we offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to meet the needs of a diverse workforce!

Flexibility: Our Hybrid with Flexibility approach combines a balance of remote working with in-office collaboration to spark teamwork and creativity.
Comprehensive benefits designed to meet your unique needs: Medical, dental, vision, access to doctors virtually, a flexible spending account to manage your health and dependent care expenses, and life and disability insurance are a small part of our offerings.
Time to recharge and energize: Generous paid time off policy - including vacation, sick, personal, and paid holidays, parental leave, and a paid winter recess.
Plan for your future financially and professionally: 401(k) with employer matching (up to 6.5%), promotional and growth opportunities, Learning and Development programs to learn on the job, and up to $7,000 for tuition reimbursement.
Mental and emotional wellness: Resources for overall well-being, including mental health and meditation benefits.
Other cool perks: A personalized health management program, pet insurance, commuter benefits, identity theft protection, discounts with our network of partners, and fun events are just a few of the optional benefits available.

The expected range for the annual base salary for this position is $85,000 - 105,000.
This role is eligible for an Incentive Compensation Plan (ICP) bonus up to 10%. This range does not include any additional pay or benefits for which a person may qualify. The actual base salary offered is determined by several variables, including, as appropriate, the applicant's qualifications for the position, the years of relevant experience, their unique skills, and the location from which they will be performing the job.

Come One, Come All

We strongly encourage you to apply if you’re interested; we'd love to learn how you can “serve” our team with your unique experience!

Position/Program Information

LOS ANGELS COUNTY

DEPARTMENT OF ARTS AND CULTURE

_____________________________________________________________________

Why work for us?

With almost 10 million residents, Los Angeles County is the most populous county in the nation! As the largest employer in Southern California with over 100,000 employees in 39 departments, we provide vital and diverse public services like law enforcement, property assessment, public health protection, water conservation, and cultural activities.

The County has more than 2100 different job types, offering a lifetime of opportunities and careers! We are dedicated professionals committed to preserving the dignity and integrity of the workplace as well as protecting the rights of each employee. Join us and discover one of the strongest public-sector benefits packages in the country with a rich selection of health care options, robust retirement plans and the flexibility to reach your fullest personal and professional potential.

For more information about our amazing employee benefits, please visit us here: https://hr.lacounty.gov/benefits/

About the Los Angeles County Department of Arts and Culture:

The mission of the Department of Arts and Culture is to advance arts, culture, and creativity throughout Los Angeles County. We provide leadership, services, and support in areas including grants and technical assistance for nonprofit organizations, countywide arts education initiatives, commissioning and care for civic art collections, research and evaluation, access to creative pathways, professional development, free community programs, and cross sector creative strategies that address civic issues. All of this work is framed by our longstanding commitment to fostering access to the arts and the County’s Cultural Equity and Inclusion Initiative. For more information about our work, partnerships, and opportunities, please visit us here: https://lacountyarts.org/

The Team Member We Are Searching For

The Department of Arts and Culture is seeking well-qualified individuals to fill Manager, Arts and Culture vacancies throughout the department. These individuals will manage and supervise, through support staff, the development, implementation, and administrative activities of a portfolio of comprehensive, highly complex, multi-layered initiatives, and specialized arts and culture programs.

The ideal candidates will have professional experience within the Los Angeles County arts and culture ecosystem, including familiarity with local arts policies, initiatives, and community needs. The Department is also seeking individuals with experience related to cultural equity, diversity, inclusion, and/or experience working with underserved communities or populations.

Our office is located at the Kenneth Hahn Hall of Administration – 500 W. Temple Street Room B-79-2 Los Angeles, CA 90012. This position is eligible for a hybrid telework arrangement.

Withhold Information

No withhold will be allowed. Required education and experience must be fully met at the time of filing, and clearly indicated on the application.

Out Of Class

Out of Class experience will not be accepted.

Essential Job Functions

What does a Manager, Arts and Culture do?

The duties listed below are intended only as an illustration of the various types of work that may be performed by a Manager, Arts and Culture. Specific duties and tasks may vary based on the assigned Division or Unit.

Oversees the establishment, implementation, and management of Department programs and initiatives.
Provides oversight of the day-to-day operations of a Division or program, including management of the operational, financial and administrative activities.
Oversees the implementation of the Division or program goals, ensuring that assigned projects and programs are effective, compliant and in line with the mission and vision of the Department and support goals of diversity, equity and inclusion.
Oversees and manages Division and program financial activities, including development and management of budgets, developing spending projections, oversight of financial tracking, accounting, and maintenance of financial and payment records for assigned programs.
Evaluates the effectiveness of programs or services and develops and implements procedural or system recommendations to optimize operational systems, processes and policies, reporting, information flow and business processes. Ensures programs are completed within budget, on time, and in compliance with policies, procedures, guidelines, and strategies that govern program initiatives.
Oversees the research and analysis of federal, state, and local laws and regulations, as well as relevant research and trends, pertaining to the assigned Division or program. Includes developing risk assessments and making recommendations to address any potential impact or opportunities.
Oversees the contracting and solicitation processes of the assigned Division or program, including developing budgets and scopes of services and overseeing contract and solicitation monitoring to ensure compliance with department policies and guidelines as well as relevant state and federal funding guidelines.
Provides technical support and administrative supervision to staff and/or consultants, including guidance on Department policy, processes, systems, operations, administration, finance, budget, contracting and purchasing. Support may also include building project plans and timelines, setting clear performance standards, reviewing work products, providing guidance and direction, and training to ensure compliance with department and County work expectations.
Represents the department at public events and meetings, and makes public presentations at program-related events, symposiums, and workshops to increase public awareness of the assigned Division or programs.
Serves as a liaison with Arts Commissioners, Board Deputies, County departments, and other government agencies, community groups, and private organizations for assigned programs and/or grants.
Facilitates and oversees marketing and outreach efforts to increase public awareness of department programs and services by promoting community involvement, coordinating special events, and developing educational and marketing materials for related department programs, projects, and initiatives.
Prepares detailed program/project status reports and specialized documents/materials as requested by Department leadership.
Responds to and resolves complex and high priority inquiries from Department contractors, grantees, artists, consultants, students, and other external stakeholders regarding program services and related issues.
May support and/or lead special projects, as directed by the Department Director or Chief Deputy.

Desirable Qualifications

Experience designing, implementing, and/or leading multi-layered programs or initiatives for organizations that provide performing arts, visual art, public art, art collections, arts education, grant-making, research and evaluation, and/or similar programs.
Demonstrated leadership experience overseeing operations, including managing staff, directing day-to-day activities, or improving organizational systems or workflows in an arts and culture or related organization or agency.
Experience in financial or contract management, which may include budgeting, fiscal oversight, contract monitoring, and managing complex funding sources.

Requirements

Who We Are

We are Tennis! The USTA (United States Tennis Association) is the national governing body for the sport of tennis and the leader in promoting and developing the sport’s growth on every level in the United States, from local communities to the crown jewel of the professional game, the US Open.

The USTA Foundation Incorporated (USTAF or USTA Foundation) is the social impact arm of the United States Tennis Association Incorporated (USTA), utilizing the powerful combination of tennis and education to enhance the lives of under-resourced youth through its support of the National Junior Tennis & Learning (NJTL) network. For more than 50 years, NJTL has impacted thousands of under-resourced youth across the nation, and today the network features more than 270 chapters that reach more than 233,000,000 young people from under-resourced communities annually.

Why Work for the USTA?

We are a passionate team of staff and volunteers focused on growing the sport of tennis and making it accessible to all. We are committed to removing barriers and creating opportunities for ALL to participate.

About Lulu's Place

Lulu's Place will offer state-of-the-art facilities in Los Angeles, north of LAX airport, between the communities of Westchester and Playa del Rey, bringing together academic, athletic, and wellness programs for youth from all backgrounds. Trusted partners, including TGR Foundation, a Tiger Woods charity; the United States Tennis Association (USTA) and its charitable arm, USTA Foundation; Cedars-Sinai; and Providence will bring together professional teachers, coaches, mentors, and service providers to deliver high-quality programs to children and their families.

The vision for this project is rooted in the passion and generosity of Carol "Lulu" Kimmelman, a Southern California native, former elementary school teacher in South Los Angeles, and lifelong tennis player who passed away in 2017 after a courageous battle with ovarian cancer. Today, her husband, Doug Kimmelman, and their four children honor Lulu's legacy by advancing her mission to transform young people's lives and create greater equity in sports and education through this groundbreaking youth center.

The Role

The Program Director at Lulu’s Place will lead a youth development program focused on college and career readiness and non-degree career pathways, operating within a shared facility alongside several partner organizations. This position involves a managerial component, overseeing program staff and volunteers.

Operational Oversight: Manage day-to-day operations for USTAF Center of Innovation (CoI), ensuring all activities align with the foundation’s mission, goals, priorities, and safety standards.
Partner Integration: Lead coordination efforts with Lulu's Place Leadership, TGR Foundation, and other on-site program partners to successfully align on shared goals and execution of educational and tennis programming.
Program Development: Lead design and oversee the planning and implementation for direct day, weekend, and afterschool programming. The programs will incorporate the core principles of the NJTL network, tennis, education, and mentorship
Community Engagement: Sets the strategy and is responsible for the USTAF CoI engagement with local community partners, including greater LA NJTL organizations, school districts, charter schools, youth development organizations, and other key community stakeholders.
Quality Assurance: Responsible for the oversight and delivery of USTAF programs and partnered programs to accomplish established and shared goals.
Strategic Growth: Identify opportunities to test and expand programs/products to increase the reach and enhance the impact of NJTL sports-based interventions within the community.

Partner & Facility Coordination

Stakeholder Liaison: Serve as the primary point of contact for diverse community partners, including non-profits, schools, and local NJTL organizations.
Facility Scheduling: Work with the Lulu’s Place facility team and partners to manage the complex master calendars for shared facility use, balancing USTAF programming needs with Lulu's Place partners and community access.
Collaborative Governance: Represent the USTAF by attending all regular partner meetings to ensure effective, efficient communication, align priorities, and minimize confusion and conflicts.
Resource Allocation: Responsible for the USTAF offices and footprint at Lulu's Place.

Impact Measurement & Reporting

Data Collection: Implement systems to track participant attendance, demographic data, and youth development outcomes across all partner programs.
Align with the USTAF leadership in the development of the “measures of success” and align with Lulu's Place partners to align on shared goals

Reporting: Capture and deliver program data into reports for foundation leadership, donors, and community stakeholders.
Evaluation: Use qualitative and quantitative feedback to assess the effectiveness of the "collective impact" model at the facility site.

Compliance & Administration

Safety & Risk Management: Ensure all partners and staff meet Safe Play compliance per the USTA requirements, including regular training and background checks. Ideally, all USTAF staff and program partners will be CPR/First Aid certified, including AED.
Budget Oversight: Manage the USTAF operational budget in collaboration with the leadership of the Programs and Services team of the USTA Foundation.
Grant Compliance: Assist partners in meeting the reporting requirements and performance benchmarks tied to USTA Foundation Program activities and funding
Ensure the program's compliance with all applicable Lulu’s Place youth safety policies, background check requirements, and licensing standards
Establish and oversee data collection, record-keeping, and reporting systems for student participation and outcomes across all program functions
Oversee vendor and service provider relationships (transportation, curriculum materials, technology, etc.)
In addition to the stated compliance and administration duties, review and maintain organizational policies and procedures, updating as needed to reflect best practices and legal requirements
Manage three full-time direct reports

Who You Are

Education: A bachelor’s degree in a related field such as Sports Management, Recreation Administration, Education, Social Work, or Non-Profit Management is required.
Work Experience: 5 to 7 years of experience in program coordination, youth development, or sports administration. Tennis background and/or understanding of the tennis environment is preferred.
Partner Management: Proven track record of managing relationships with community partners, schools, or diverse local organizations is required.
Safety Certifications: Valid CPR, First Aid, and AED certifications (or the ability to obtain them within 30 days of hire) are required.
Clearance: Ability to pass comprehensive, recurring federal and state background checks to work with minors is required.
Technical Proficiency: Strong skills in Microsoft Office Suite (especially Excel), Google Workspace, and familiarity with project management or participant tracking software are required.
Valid driver’s license and reliable transportation for travel between facility sites is required.
Schedule Flexibility: Ability to work non-traditional hours, including evenings and weekends, to align with youth sports schedules is required.
Physical Stamina: Ability to be mobile and active on sports courts or fields for extended periods and lift/move equipment up to 50 lbs is required.

What We Offer

At the USTA, we know people are our most important asset. For this reason, we offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to meet the needs of a diverse workforce!

Flexibility: Our Hybrid with Flexibility approach combines a balance of remote working with in-office collaboration to spark teamwork and creativity.
Comprehensive benefits designed to meet your unique needs: Medical, dental, vision, access to doctors virtually, a flexible spending account to manage your health and dependent care expenses, and life and disability insurance are a small part of our offerings.
Time to recharge and energize: Generous paid time off policy - including vacation, sick, personal, and paid holidays, parental leave, and a paid winter recess.
Plan for your future financially and professionally: 401(k) with employer matching (up to 6.5%), promotional and growth opportunities, Learning and Development programs to learn on the job, and up to $7,000 for tuition reimbursement.
Mental and emotional wellness: Resources for overall well-being, including mental health and meditation benefits.
Other cool perks: A personalized health management program, pet insurance, commuter benefits, identity theft protection, discounts with our network of partners, and fun events are just a few of the optional benefits available.

The actual base salary offered is determined by several variables, including, as appropriate, the applicant's qualifications for the position, the years of relevant experience, their unique skills, and the location from which they will be performing the job.

Position/Program Information

LOS ANGELS COUNTY

DEPARTMENT OF ARTS AND CULTURE

When To Apply

RT8811B

Type Of Recruitment

We welcome applications from everyone.

_____________________________________________________________________

Why work for us?

With almost 10 million residents, Los Angeles County is the most populous county in the nation! As the largest employer in Southern California with over 100,000 employees in 39 departments, we provide vital and diverse public services like law enforcement, property assessment, public health protection, water conservation, and cultural activities.

The County has more than 2100 different job types, offering a lifetime of opportunities and careers! We are dedicated professionals committed to preserving the dignity and integrity of the workplace as well as protecting the rights of each employee. Join us and discover one of the strongest public-sector benefits packages in the country with a rich selection of health care options, robust retirement plans and the flexibility to reach your fullest personal and professional potential.

For more information about our amazing employee benefits, please visit us here: https://hr.lacounty.gov/benefits/

About the Los Angeles County Department of Arts and Culture:

The mission of the Department of Arts and Culture is to advance arts, culture, and creativity throughout Los Angeles County. We provide leadership, services, and support in areas including grants and technical assistance for nonprofit organizations, countywide arts education initiatives, commissioning and care for civic art collections, research and evaluation, access to creative pathways, professional development, free community programs, and cross sector creative strategies that address civic issues. All of this work is framed by our longstanding commitment to fostering access to the arts and the County’s Cultural Equity and Inclusion Initiative. For more information about our work, partnerships, and opportunities, please visit us here: https://lacountyarts.org/

The Team Member We Are Searching For

The Department of Arts and Culture is seeking well-qualified individuals to fill Manager, Arts and Culture vacancies throughout the department. These individuals will manage and supervise, through support staff, the development, implementation, and administrative activities of a portfolio of comprehensive, highly complex, multi-layered initiatives, and specialized arts and culture programs.

The ideal candidates will have professional experience within the Los Angeles County arts and culture ecosystem, including familiarity with local arts policies, initiatives, and community needs. The Department is also seeking individuals with experience related to cultural equity, diversity, inclusion, and/or experience working with underserved communities or populations.

Our office is located at the Kenneth Hahn Hall of Administration – 500 W. Temple Street Room B-79-2 Los Angeles, CA 90012. This position is eligible for a hybrid telework arrangement.

Withhold Information

No withhold will be allowed. Required education and experience must be fully met at the time of filing, and clearly indicated on the application.

Out Of Class

Out of Class experience will not be accepted.

Essential Job Functions

What does a Manager, Arts and Culture do?

The duties listed below are intended only as an illustration of the various types of work that may be performed by a Manager, Arts and Culture. Specific duties and tasks may vary based on the assigned Division or Unit.

Oversees the establishment, implementation, and management of Department programs and initiatives.
Provides oversight of the day-to-day operations of a Division or program, including management of the operational, financial and administrative activities.
Oversees the implementation of the Division or program goals, ensuring that assigned projects and programs are effective, compliant and in line with the mission and vision of the Department and support goals of diversity, equity and inclusion.
Oversees and manages Division and program financial activities, including development and management of budgets, developing spending projections, oversight of financial tracking, accounting, and maintenance of financial and payment records for assigned programs.
Evaluates the effectiveness of programs or services and develops and implements procedural or system recommendations to optimize operational systems, processes and policies, reporting, information flow and business processes. Ensures programs are completed within budget, on time, and in compliance with policies, procedures, guidelines, and strategies that govern program initiatives.
Oversees the research and analysis of federal, state, and local laws and regulations, as well as relevant research and trends, pertaining to the assigned Division or program. Includes developing risk assessments and making recommendations to address any potential impact or opportunities.
Oversees the contracting and solicitation processes of the assigned Division or program, including developing budgets and scopes of services and overseeing contract and solicitation monitoring to ensure compliance with department policies and guidelines as well as relevant state and federal funding guidelines.
Provides technical support and administrative supervision to staff and/or consultants, including guidance on Department policy, processes, systems, operations, administration, finance, budget, contracting and purchasing. Support may also include building project plans and timelines, setting clear performance standards, reviewing work products, providing guidance and direction, and training to ensure compliance with department and County work expectations.
Represents the department at public events and meetings, and makes public presentations at program-related events, symposiums, and workshops to increase public awareness of the assigned Division or programs.
Serves as a liaison with Arts Commissioners, Board Deputies, County departments, and other government agencies, community groups, and private organizations for assigned programs and/or grants.
Facilitates and oversees marketing and outreach efforts to increase public awareness of department programs and services by promoting community involvement, coordinating special events, and developing educational and marketing materials for related department programs, projects, and initiatives.
Prepares detailed program/project status reports and specialized documents/materials as requested by Department leadership.
Responds to and resolves complex and high priority inquiries from Department contractors, grantees, artists, consultants, students, and other external stakeholders regarding program services and related issues.
May support and/or lead special projects, as directed by the Department Director or Chief Deputy.

Desirable Qualifications

Experience designing, implementing, and/or leading multi-layered programs or initiatives for organizations that provide performing arts, visual art, public art, art collections, arts education, grant-making, research and evaluation, and/or similar programs.
Demonstrated leadership experience overseeing operations, including managing staff, directing day-to-day activities, or improving organizational systems or workflows in an arts and culture or related organization or agency.
Experience in financial or contract management, which may include budgeting, fiscal oversight, contract monitoring, and managing complex funding sources.

Requirements

Requirements to Qualify:

Option 1

A Bachelor’s Degree or higher from an accredited college or university in Public or Business Administration, Arts Administration, Education, or a related field* -AND- one (1) year** of program management experience*** at the level of**** the Los Angeles County classification of Senior Program Associate, Arts and Culture*****.

Option 2

A Bachelor’s Degree or higher from an accredited college or university in Public or Business Administration, Arts Administration, Education, or a related field* -AND- three (3) years** of program management experience*** at the level of**** the Los Angeles County classification of Program Associate, Arts and Culture******.

License

A valid California Class C Driver License or the ability to use an alternative method of transportation when needed to carry out job-related essential functions.

Physical Class

2 – Light: This class includes administrative and clerical positions requiring light physical effort that may include occasional light lifting to a 10-pound limit and some bending, stooping, or squatting. Considerable ambulation may be involved.

Special Requirements Information

To receive credit for your education, include a legible copy of all relevant official documents including your diploma, transcripts, or letter/certificate from an accredited institution or email it to careers@arts.lacounty.gov within seven (7) days of the end of the filing period. The document should show the date the degree was conferred and be in English. If not in English, then translation is required. International degrees must be evaluated for equivalency to U.S. standards if not listed in the International Handbook of Universities or World Higher Education Database. Documents marked as unofficial will not be accepted. For more information on our standards for educational documents, please visit: https://file.lacounty.gov/SDSInter/dhr/070812_PPG123.pdf and https://file.lacounty.gov/SDSInter/dhr/205105_PPG_123_ACE_Resource_Guide.pdf .

We do not accept password-protected documents. Ensure documents are unlocked before attaching to your application or sending to the exam analyst.

Full-time experience will be evaluated on the basis of a 40-hour work week. Part-time experience will be evaluated and prorated accordingly.
Program Management Experience is defined as: Experience with establishing program goals and providing direction to achieve program objectives; establishing and executing plans to achieve program outcomes; developing and/or implementing projects or programs, systems and procedures; establishing schedules, priorities, and performance standards for program activities; coordinating and monitoring program activities to ensure they are carried out efficiently and effectively; overseeing budget activities and conducting fiscal planning and monitoring to support program operations
At the level: You may still qualify even if your job title isn’t exactly the same as the ones listed. What matters is that your experience is at a similar level — meaning your job involves similar responsibilities, requires comparable skills and knowledge, and takes place within a similar organizational structure. Please provide a clear explanation of your experience to demonstrate that it is at the appropriate level.
Senior Program Associate, Arts and Culture is defined as: Manages and oversees the planning, development, analysis, and administrative activities of a Department of Arts and Culture project or a small program.
Program Associate, Arts and Culture is defined as: Provides specialized technical program support and administrative, fiscal, and project management services for professional personnel involved in the development and implementation of a comprehensive Department of Arts and Culture program.

This examination will consist of an Evaluation of Education and Experience, weighted 100%, based on application information, Desirable Qualifications and responses to the Supplemental Questionnaire.

About the Opportunity

The organization is seeking a full-time, 100% remote Director of Operations
to lead and scale its operations department. Reporting directly to the Chief Operating Officer, this senior leadership position is critical to organizational growth and financial health. The Director of Operations will drive strategic operations, lead a high-performing team, and partner with executive leadership across the organization to ensure operational excellence and sound financial governance.

The ideal candidate combines strategic thinking with hands-on execution, brings fiscal discipline and analytical rigor to complex decisions, and excels at building trust and alignment across teams while navigating ambiguity in a mission-driven nonprofit environment.

Key Responsibilities

Human Resources & Talent Management:
Design and implement hiring processes that attract and retain top talent.
Guide salary negotiations.
Partner with managers to manage staff performance and assist with team development.
Oversee annual performance review processes and training programs for managers.
Integrate organizational core values into all stages of the employee life cycle.
Review benefits structures, recommend updates, and oversee benefits administration.
Own the organization's compensation philosophy and structure.
Manage payroll systems and ensure tax and regulatory requirements are met.
Oversee contract labor acquisition, maintain contractor records, and report on key contractor metrics.

Finance, Budget & Financial Leadership:
Develop and maintain financial dashboards tracking key metrics.
Produce monthly financial reports translating data into actionable insights and strategic implications.
Monitor financial health and proactively flag risks and opportunities.
Build financial models to evaluate ROI on expansion initiatives and strategic investments before implementation.
Lead annual budget development.
Develop rolling cash flow forecasts and scenario models to inform reserve strategy and proactive financial decision-making.
Oversee all financial operations, including accounting, payroll, accounts payable/receivable, cash management, and financial compliance.

Maintain state and federal compliance, proactively identifying new legal and regulatory requirements.
Maintain workers' compensation policies at national and state levels, ensuring no lapses in required registrations or insurance.
Coordinate FMLA, ADA, and other compliance-related processes, identifying new laws that may impact the organization.
Manage legal claims and lawsuits, coordinating with outside counsel on contract reviews and personnel matters.
Maintain organizational insurance policies and make recommendations on coverage adjustments.

Department Leadership & Administration:
Mentor, coach, and develop operations department personnel.
Schedule and facilitate departmental meetings and oversee annual and quarterly goals.
Maintain organizational systems and tools, managing user access and permissions across platforms.
Supervise the planning of board meetings and coordinate in-person team meetings.

Strong understanding of and experience in human resources, talent management, and organizational development.

Strategic thinking skills combining analytical rigor with practical problem-solving and proactive decision-making.
Excellent communication skills with the ability to articulate complex concepts clearly and build alignment across teams.
Comfort with ambiguity and the ability to navigate change in a fast-moving nonprofit environment.
Deep commitment to the organization's mission and a demonstrated ability to exemplify organizational values.
Experience with Google Workspace, Slack, and project management tools.

Interest in or experience with artificial intelligence tools.

This is a full-time, 100% remote position based in the United States, with work conducted from a home office. The organization provides a flexible work environment with flexible scheduling.

new_jobs.title: Development Director
new_jobs.description:
Overview

Since our founding in 1924, we've cut cardiovascular disease deaths in half, but there is still so much more to do. To overcome today’s biggest health challenges and accelerate this progress, we need passionate individuals like you. Join our movement, be part of the progress, and help ensure a healthier future for all. You matter, and so does the impact you can make with us.

We're looking for a dynamic, relationship-driven Development Director to lead our suite of competitive fundraising campaigns, including Leaders of Impact, Woman of Impact, and Teen of Impact
, across Oregon and Southwest Washington.

This is a highly visible, community-facing role for someone who thrives on building authentic relationships, connecting people to purpose, and inspiring others to achieve ambitious goals. You will identify and recruit influential changemakers, business leaders, philanthropists, and emerging community leaders, helping them amplify their impact through fundraising, awareness-building, and volunteer leadership while advancing the American Heart Association's mission.

Success in this role requires a proactive networker who enjoys meeting new people, uncovering opportunities, and creating meaningful volunteer experiences. You'll serve as a trusted coach, connector, and champion for volunteers while building a year-round pipeline of changemakers and future volunteer leaders.

This field-based role requires travel throughout the greater Portland and Vancouver area.

Why You'll Love This Role

Join a mission-driven organization where your work has a visible impact on communities across Oregon and Southwest Washington.
Build meaningful relationships with some of the most influential leaders and changemakers in our community.
Help volunteers raise funds and awareness that directly support lifesaving work.
Play a key role in developing the next generation of American Heart Association volunteers and leaders.
Be part of a collaborative team that is advancing health and hope for everyone, everywhere.

We have a fast-paced sales type of environment with the main responsibility of driving revenue in support of our mission. We offer a base salary with the potential to earn an incentive up to 25% of your base pay. The potential incentive is based on achieving certain revenue targets and triggers.

The Association offers many resources to help you maintain work-life harmonization through your changing needs and life situations. To help you be successful, you will have access to Heart U, our award-winning corporate university, as well as additional training and support, locally.

\#TheAHALife is more than a company culture; it is our way of life. It embodies our commitment to work-life harmonization and is guided by our core values where our employees can thrive both personally and professionally. Discover why you will Be Seen. Be Heard. Be Valued at the American Heart Association by following us on LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X, and at heart.jobs.

Responsibilities

Recruit and Inspire Community Changemakers

Identify and engage individuals with the potential to create significant impact through fundraising, awareness-building, community influence, and long-term volunteer leadership.
Build relationships across business, philanthropic, and community networks to continuously expand campaign reach and visibility.
Cast a wide net to identify future nominees and develop a sustainable pipeline of high-potential volunteers and supporters.

Drive Campaign Growth and Revenue

Lead fundraising strategies for Leaders of Impact, Woman of Impact, and Teen of Impact campaigns to achieve and exceed revenue goals.
Conduct year-round prospecting, networking, and relationship-building activities to identify, recruit, and secure high-impact campaign participants and supporters.
Secure financial contributions through exploratory meetings, sponsorship conversations, and revenue-generating sales calls.
Develop and execute year-round plans that establish a strong pipeline of nominees, sponsors, and volunteers well in advance of campaign launches.

Coach and Support Volunteers

Provide exceptional, personalized support to campaign participants throughout their fundraising journey, ensuring they are valued, celebrated, and set up for success.
Build trust and rapport quickly, serving as an advisor, coach, and motivator.
Deliver effective orientation, training, fundraising guidance, and ongoing support to help volunteers maximize their impact and success.
Foster meaningful volunteer experiences that strengthen long-term engagement with the American Heart Association.

Develop Long-Term Leadership Engagement

Cultivate relationships with volunteers beyond individual campaigns by connecting them to additional volunteer leadership opportunities.
Create pathways for ongoing volunteer engagement across the organization.
Recognize and celebrate volunteer contributions through meaningful stewardship and engagement activities.

Collaborate Across the Market

Partner closely with internal colleagues across departments to identify prospective nominees, share best practices, and support overall market success.
Work collaboratively to strengthen community engagement strategies that elevate all campaigns and organizational priorities.
Communicate proactively with internal and external stakeholders to ensure exceptional relationship management and customer service.

Ensure Operational Excellence

Manage campaign and donor information accurately and timely using American Heart Association systems and tools.
Coordinate campaign events, volunteer gatherings, cultivation activities, kickoffs, and celebrations, both in-person and virtually.
Ensure compliance with all American Heart Association policies, fiscal standards, and applicable regulations.
Maintain strong attention to detail while managing multiple priorities and deadlines.

Qualifications

What Makes Someone Successful in This Role?

The Ideal Candidate Is:

Well-connected in the community or excited to become deeply immersed in local business and community networks.
Energized by coaching and encouraging others, celebrating wins, and helping volunteers reach ambitious goals.
Motivated by ambitious goals and achieving meaningful results.
Comfortable networking, prospecting, and building relationships with people from all backgrounds and industries.
Naturally curious and genuinely interested in learning about others.
A skilled relationship-builder who develops trust and rapport quickly.
Passionate about helping others discover and reach their full potential with the ability to coach, motivate, and inspire others to succeed.
Confident engaging executives, business owners, volunteer leaders, and community influencers.
Collaborative and team-oriented, with a mindset focused on lifting the success of the entire market.
Strategic, forward-thinking, and always looking for opportunities to expand impact.
Highly organized with exceptional follow-through and attention to detail.
Compassionate, service-oriented, and committed to creating exceptional volunteer experiences.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
Minimum of three (3) years of success in fundraising, sales, business development, account management, volunteer engagement, community outreach, or a related relationship-driven field. Recent graduates welcome and encouraged to apply.
Experience motivating individuals or teams to achieve significant fundraising, sales, or business-development goals.
Track record of building long-term partnerships and expanding community engagement through relationship-based strategies.
Demonstrated success achieving ambitious goals through relationship-building, influence, and personal accountability.
Ability to build trust and establish meaningful relationships across audiences.
Strong written, verbal, presentation, and interpersonal communication skills.
Ability to work independently while effectively managing multiple projects and priorities.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications.
Ability to travel locally up to 75% of the time, with occasional overnight travel as needed.
Access to reliable transportation.
Ability to lift and/or move materials and event supplies as needed, with appropriate assistance when required.

Preferred Experience

Experience recruiting, managing, or cultivating executive leaders, business owners, philanthropists, or influential volunteers.
Knowledge of corporate, nonprofit, philanthropic, and community networks throughout Oregon and Southwest Washington.
Experience in peer-to-peer fundraising, volunteer engagement, community outreach, or consultative sales.

Compensation & Benefits

The American Heart Association invests in its people. Here are the main components of our total rewards package. Visit Rewards & Benefits to see more details.

Compensation – Our goal is to ensure you have a competitive base salary. That’s why we regularly review the market value of jobs and make adjustments, as needed.
Performance and Recognition – You are rewarded for achieving success through annual salary planning and incentive programs; this position is incentive eligible based on achieving certain targets.
Benefits – We offer a wide array of benefits including medical, dental, vision, disability, and life insurance, along with a robust retirement program that includes an employer match and automatic contribution. As a mark of our commitment to employee well-being, we also offer an employee assistance program, employee wellness program and telemedicine, and medical consultation.
Professional Development – You can join one of our many Employee Resource Groups (ERG) or be a mentor/mentee in our professional mentoring program. Heart U is the Association’s national online university, with more than 100,000 resources designed to meet your needs and busy schedule.
Work-Life Harmonization – The Association offers Paid Time Off (PTO) at a minimum of 16 days per year for new employees. The number of days will increase based on seniority level. You will also have a total of 12 paid holidays off each year, which includes several days off at the end of the year.
Tuition Assistance - We support the career development of all employees. This program provides financial assistance to employees who wish to further their education and career in relation to their current duties and responsibilities, or for potential future positions in the organization.

The American Heart Association’s 2028 Goal: Building on over 100 years of trusted leadership in cardiovascular and brain health, by 2028 the Association will drive breakthroughs and implement proven solutions in science, policy, and care for healthier people and communities. The greatest discoveries in health must reach everyone where they are.

At American Heart Association | American Stroke Association, our mission is to be a relentless force for a world of longer, healthier lives, regardless of race, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, religion, age, language, sexual orientation, national origin and physical or cognitive abilities.

Director, Strategic Engagement

Ready to help shape the future of the insurance industry?

Aon Inpoint advises insurers and reinsurers across the Property & Casualty and Health & Benefits marketplace. Through analytics, advisory services, and industry expertise, we help clients address complex challenges and make informed decisions.

We're looking for a Director, Strategic Engagement to join our North America team. This role plays an important part in expanding client relationships, supporting business growth, and connecting clients with the expertise and resources needed to achieve their goals.

What You'll Do

Build Client Relationships & Grow Business

Develop and strengthen relationships with senior leaders across the insurance sector.
Identify client priorities, identify areas for growth, and help shape advisory engagements that address pressing business challenges.
Support business development efforts that expand Aon Inpoint's presence and client results across North America.
Participate in commercial discussions, proposal development, contract negotiations, and engagement planning activities.

Deliver Strategic Insight

Apply market research, industry knowledge, analytics, and Aon's global capabilities to help clients navigatechanging market conditions.
Provide business advice that helps clients improve performance, manage risk, and pursue growth opportunities.
Monitor market trends, competitive activity, and emerging industry developments to inform recommendations.

Support Key Initiatives

Partner with NFP Broking leadership and Aon colleagues to support integration activities, expand collaboration, and identify opportunities across both organizations.
Lead complex client engagements and cross-functional initiatives, coordinating resources, timelines, and priorities to achieve desired results.
Identify opportunities to improve processes, enhance service delivery, and create a stronger client experience.

Lead & Develop Talent

Contribute to a collaborative and inclusive team environment where colleagues can learn, develop, and grow.
Provide coaching, feedback, and support to help team members strengthen their capabilities and achieve their goals.
Help attract, develop, and retain strong talent across the business.

What We're Looking For

15+ years of experience in the insurance industry, primarily in carrier-facing roles.
Experience in broking, consulting, advisory, engagement, or other client-facing strategic leadership environments.
Track record of developing executive-level relationships and generating new business opportunities.
Strong understanding of insurance market dynamics, carrier operations, and industry challenges.
Experience leading projects, managing competing priorities, and working across multiple stakeholder groups.
Exceptional communication, relationship-building, negotiation, and influencing skills.
Experience developing talent and leading high-performing teams.
Ability to analyze business issues, evaluate risk, and translate insights into practical recommendations.
Strong judgment, problem-solving ability, and organizational leadership skills.
Willingness to travel approximately 20%.

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience.
Advanced degree preferred.
Experience working within large, matrixed organizations.
Experience using CRM platforms to manage client relationships and business development activities.

Why Join Aon Inpoint?

Work with leading insurers and reinsurers across North America while helping clients address important business challenges. Collaborate with experienced colleagues, contribute to major client engagements, and play a meaningful role in the continued growth of Aon Inpoint!

For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances.

Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate.

Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time.

The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $200,000 - $270,000 annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location.

This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon’s annual incentive plans to receive an annual discretionary bonus in addition to base salary. The amount of any bonus varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan.

Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance. This role does not accrue vacation. Rather, this role is eligible to take paid time off at the discretion of the employee and management in accordance with company policy and practices. Various other types of leaves of absence; paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies.
